item.title: Pistons hit first road bump on four-game trip in loss to Heat
item.description: The Detroit Pistons fell to the Miami Heat , 137-117, on Saturday, Nov. 14, at the Kaseya Center. The game also marked the Pistons' second road loss this season, bringing their record to 8-4 overall. The Pistons have remained competitive without All-NBA center Jalen Duren, who suffered a hamstring strain on Oct. 23 against the Heat. Although he is making progress in his recovery, Duren is expected to miss at least two more weeks. BOX SCORE: Heat 137, Pistons 117 After their 144-140 double-overtime victory over the Washington Wizards on Thursday, Nov. 12, the Pistons improved to 6-3 without Duren. However, it is becoming increasingly evident that they miss his skills. The game against the Heat highlighted the impact of Duren's absence and what the Pistons have been missing, as they took advantage of Detroit's lack of size more than Washington did. Cade Cunningham followed up his historic 52-point, 11-assist performance against the Wizards with 33 points, eight assists and five rebounds. Kevin Huerter added 20 points. Giannis Antetokounmpo led the way for Miami with 34 points, 14 rebounds and eight assists. Klay Thompson added 26 points with six made triples. Observations and notes ▶ A rough night for Thompson : Cunningham performed well, continuing his strong play from two nights ago, but the same isn't true for Ausar Thompson. Foul trouble in the first half limited his time on the court and kept him from contributing effectively. He picked up a pair of fouls within the first two minutes of the first quarter. At the start of the second quarter, Thompson committed an offensive foul at the 11:08 mark. ▶ Robinson exits with thigh injury : Duncan Robinson's evening ended early due to left thigh soreness, which occurred midway through the second quarter. The injury was particularly unfortunate, as he had been one of the Pistons' most dependable offensive players at that point. Robinson finished with 10 points, including two made 3-pointers, in just 16 minutes. coty.davis@detroitnews.com @cotydavis_24 This article originally appeared on The Detroit News: Pistons hit first road bump on four-game trip in loss to Heat

And Becker dropped a poignant message to Hoosiers nation after the win. Wide receiver Charlie Becker walked out of Memorial Stadium pointing to the student section. item.title: Hocevar And Cleetus Win LeMullets In Epic Crown Vic Clash
item.description: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images The pair took home the 2026 2.4 Hours of LeMullets title at the Freedom Factory in Bradenton, Florida. Motorsport.com NASCAR Cup reported the event ended with a dramatic showdown that left fans cheering and cars smashed. The race turned into a full-contact brawl involving old Ford Crown Vics. Hocevar pushed Ty Dillon aside just as the white flag flew to seize the lead. Dillon tried to fight back into Turn 1 but ran wide and nearly hit a tractor tire trying to slow down for the chicane. Hocevar surged ahead while sliding sideways and making slight contact with the #10 car. The crowd roared as Hocevar held on to win ahead of Dillon, who was sharing his car with his father Mike. Denny Hamlin and Alex Presley finished third after a late charge through the mess. The Crash Was The Best Part Hocevar joked about the damage. He said, “Yeah, I’m glad it was the front bumper — the back bumper was pretty expensive last time I used that,” referencing a brake-check incident from a Cup race that got him suspended. He admitted, “So, that was a lot of fun,” and added, “It was fun beating up with these guys. I ran into a lot of guys I have all season, but they’re laughing about it now. So, this is a lot of fun. So, I appreciate that man.” Cleetus McFarland called Hocevar a “cheat code,” saying all he had to do was “drive safely for 35 minutes.” Ryan Preece, full of smiles, went over to congratulate Hocevar after Hocevar spun into the tires on the backstretch. Bug Strmiska survived a rollover crash, then stood on the inverted vehicle and thrust his fists upward toward the sky. NASCAR Stars Embrace The Chaos Heavy.com noted that the NASCAR season may be over, but big names like Hamlin, Hocevar, Preece, and Ty Dillon weren’t done racing yet. They traded their usual high-tech race cars for nitrous-powered Crown Victorias for this unconventional endurance-style race. The event brought professional drivers, celebrities, and automotive personalities together for a wild night on the 3/8-mile asphalt oval. Fans could watch the main event at 7:30 p.m. ET on FRDM+. In the remains of his No. 11 car, Hamlin discussed his wild night. “I hit everything but the lottery, that’s for sure,” Hamlin said. This win marks the second straight year Hocevar and McFarland have taken the trophy.

item.description: MIAMI — Mauricio Pochettino's days with the U.S. national team are almost over, a bittersweet conclusion to an adventure that carried through one stimulating World Cup but, because of Manchester United's irresistible allure, will fall years short of another. Before he can head off to Old Trafford, though, he must complete the final assignment of his 26-month tenure: the CONCACAF Nations League quarterfinals. Any concerns the week-long sideshow would lead the U.S. astray were extinguished in Saturday's first leg at Nu Stadium. Two days after Pochettino told them he had accepted United's offer, the Americans performed with purpose and panache in a 6-0 drubbing of Haiti . Yes, Haiti was horrible defensively. But Pochettino had his team playing quality soccer in extending the winning streak to five. "Thank you to the players, to the staff, to everyone because the commitment we showed was what we wanted from the beginning in this journey together more than two years ago," Pochettino said. "That is why I am so happy. They were very, very professional from the day they started to see all the rumors, and then when we confirmed [the United move] a few days ago … we were so proud how they managed the situation." In their first appearances since the World Cup, Christian Pulisic scored twice in a two-minute gap early in the second half, and Weston McKennie and Folarin Balogun contributed to a five-goal second half that rendered Tuesday's second leg in Cincinnati almost meaningless. Auston Trusty and teenager Julian Hall were responsible for the first two goals. Mauricio Pochettino's time with the USMNT is nearly over, but the bond he built with his players appears to be intact. JC Ruiz via Getty Images Amid the Pochettino-United saga , "We know we had a job to do," captain Tyler Adams said, "and you could see we were focused on it." "We have to respect that and understand that. It's a part of the business. I wish him all the best, and I'm very grateful for everything he's done for the national team. I've played my best football for the national team under Pochettino. He's come in and really shaken things up. I'm someone who's benefited from that." item.description: Jacob Hubert runs the ball for Glens Falls during the Section 2 Class B Super Bowl against Averill Park on Saturday at Shenendehowa. "I would be lying if I said this wasn't these guys' goal coming in," Glens Falls head coach Pat Lilac said after the title win. "Most of them have been on the two previous teams that won, and I know they would have been disappointed with anything less than a sectional title. After Averill Park took the lead in the first quarter, the two teams traded jabs in the second. "Hats off to Averill Park for their game plan," Lilac said. "They came and took it to us in the first half. They kept our offense off the field and they took away the things that we do best. item.title: Boston College’s 51 Passing Yards Tell the Story of a Brutal Loss to Notre Dame
item.description: Boston College’s 51 Passing Yards Tell the Story of a Brutal Loss to Notre Dame originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Boston College needed a response after falling behind early at Notre Dame. Instead, the Eagles spent most of Saturday trying to escape a game that was already slipping away. No. 3 Notre Dame scored 31 points before halftime and rolled to a 41-7 victory. Boston College finished with just 136 yards of offense, including 51 through the air, as the Fighting Irish controlled the game from the opening quarter. The Eagles’ lone touchdown came after one of the few moments that went their way. Boston College intercepted Notre Dame quarterback CJ Carr early in the third quarter, and Bo MacCormack III finished the short drive with a three-yard rushing score. It was MacCormack’s sixth rushing touchdown of the season, but the Eagles couldn’t build on it. Quick Response Notre Dame answered immediately with a touchdown drive of its own, then added a field goal in the fourth quarter. The Fighting Irish also got a defensive touchdown late in the first half after recovering a fumble in the end zone, turning an already difficult afternoon into a 31-0 halftime deficit. Boston College’s passing game never gained traction. Quarterback Mason McKenzie completed eight of 21 attempts for 51 yards, leaving the Eagles with little room to threaten Notre Dame’s lead. Mekhi Dodd led BC with 45 rushing yards, while MacCormack had 20 receiving yards and the team’s lone touchdown. MORE : How to Watch Boston College vs. Notre Dame: Channel, Live Stream & Start Time for College Football Game A Difficult Afternoon, and a Short Week to Respond The result drops Boston College to 4-6. The Eagles will have to quickly move on from a lopsided road loss and turn their attention to Syracuse, which visits Chestnut Hill next Saturday. The interception and touchdown offered a brief sign of life after halftime. But the overall performance made clear how much the Eagles need to improve on offense if they want to make the most of the remaining games.

item.title: Shock and Heartbreak as Beloved Broadcaster Dies At 64
item.description: Sep 29, 2016; Chaska, MN, USA; NBC hosts Dan Hicks and Michele Tafoya during the Opening Ceremony for the 41st Ryder Cup at Hazeltine National Golf Club. Mandatory Credit: Michael Madrid-USA TODAY Sports The sports world lost a giant voice this week. Dan Hicks, the man who called the biggest moments in golf and college football, died at age 64. His death came just days before he was set to broadcast a Notre Dame football game. The news broke on Thursday, leaving fans and colleagues in shock. Hicks was scheduled to call the matchup between Notre Dame and Boston College on Saturday in South Bend, Indiana. Instead, the broadcast booth will go silent for a legend. His wife, ESPN anchor Hannah Storm , confirmed the loss in a post to X. She described the passing as sudden and unexpected, citing an acute illness as the cause. No other details were released by the family. pic.twitter.com/8CK7OLXbZx — Hannah Storm (@HannahStormESPN) November 12, 2026 A Life Built on the Mic Hicks was the face and voice of NBC Sports for decades . He joined the network in 1992 and stayed until the end of his life. That stretch covers 34 years of work. He became the signature voice of NBC’s golf coverage for the last 26 years. His work included calling 27 Tiger Woods victories and 27 U.S. Opens. Beyond the greens, he handled play-by-play for multiple Olympic Games . He started with the 1992 Barcelona Games and most recently covered Alpine Skiing at the Milan Cortina Games this year. NBC Sports president Rick Cordella, along with Sam Flood and Molly Solomon, honored his career in a joint statement. “Dan Hicks was an extraordinary colleague, friend, and person,” the executives wrote. They noted that his blend of knowledge, style, and humor kept fans entertained for decades. The statement also highlighted his role as a leader who welcomed teammates with a smile or a joke. Family First Always While the world knew him as a broadcaster, Hicks loved his family the most. He and Storm have been married for over 30 years. They raised three daughters together: Hannah, Ellery, and Riley. Storm shared that the family is heartbroken by the loss. She wrote that his loss is immeasurable. Hicks often used social media to celebrate his daughters’ achievements. His last Instagram post, shared on Oct. 11, showed his daughter Riley running in the Chicago Marathon. In hot weather, she smashed her personal record, an achievement he wrote about. “Our girl did it again. 3rd major marathon in 18 months,” he wrote. That post stands as his final public message before his death on Wednesday in Connecticut. The Game That Was Never Called This season marked Hicks’ seventh year calling Notre Dame football games . item.title: Josh Allen’s backup gets unexpected Bills promotion ahead of Jets clash
item.description: Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images The Buffalo Bills have elevated quarterback Shane Buechele from their practice squad ahead of their meeting with the New York Jets, despite having Josh Allen and Kyle Allen available. The move is Buechele’s first elevation to the active roster this season, with Bills insider Sal Capaccio suggesting it is more of a reward than a response to an injury concern. Buffalo have relied on Buechele as their third quarterback for several seasons, and the decision could also offer a positive sign about the team’s wider injury situation. Buffalo Bills elevate Shane Buechele to reward his work behind Josh Allen Capaccio explained that the Bills could be giving Buechele an opportunity to earn a higher game check while making him available as their emergency third quarterback. He wrote on X: “Probably to reward him with an active roster game check for a week. This will also allow him to be the emergency 3rd QB if declared inactive (hopefully that wouldn’t be needed).” Buechele has been part of Buffalo’s practice squad for the past three seasons after initially joining the organisation following his release from the Kansas City Chiefs in 2022. The 28-year-old has also built a strong relationship with Josh Allen and is considered a valuable presence in the quarterbacks’ room. He previously returned to Kansas City when the Chiefs needed additional depth following season-ending injuries to Patrick Mahomes and Gardner Minshew. Buechele appeared in one game, completing seven of 14 passes for 88 yards. The promotion could also be encouraging news for Buffalo’s injury situation. The Bills have used practice squad elevations to cover injury concerns in recent weeks but did not call up any other players alongside Buechele. That could suggest starting right tackle Spencer Brown, who had been dealing with an injury, is in a better position. Buffalo also activated defensive back Jordan Hancock from injured reserve and released practice squad cornerback Te’Cory Couch in a separate roster move. Josh Allen is expected to remain the starter against the Jets, with Kyle Allen also available. Buechele could therefore serve as the emergency third quarterback, giving the Bills another option if both players are unable to continue. For now, his elevation appears to be recognition of his work behind the scenes rather than a sign of trouble for Buffalo’s starting quarterback. item.title: UFC 334 results: Kevin Holland and Uros Medic ends in confusing majority draw after 3 rounds
item.description: NEW YORK, NEW YORK -. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Zuffa LLC) Kevin Holland had to once again survive some groin strikes and it appeared he was heading towards victory until the judges delivered a majority draw after three rounds. Holland nearly got the win early with a D’arce choke submission but showed off some solid striking while bouncing back from the repeated fouls to get the job done. But two judges scored the fight 28-28 with the third official going 30-27 for Holland but the result is still the same with a confusing majority draw. Medic was patient early but he finally unleashed a barrage of shots that Holland did a good job of avoiding. Medic connected with a hard left hand but Holland answered right back as the exchanges continued. Holland landed a slick uppercut that got Medic’s attention as he started talking to his opponent before scoring a well-timed knockdown. Holland then locked up a D’arce choke before falling to the canvas to lock up the submission. Medic was surviving as Holland was holding onto the choke and he eventually escaped just before the opening round ended. Medic attempted to re-establish his striking in the second round as he threw out several kicks before going back up top to the head with punches. Medic connected with a hard right hand and then went back down to the body. Medic then uncorked a second kick to the groin that caused a pause in the action. Referee Marc Goddard gave him time to recover before taking a point away. On the restart, Holland was throwing plenty of kicks of his own before a quick takedown but Medic was doing his best to resist as the battle moved back to the cage.

item.title: Leistikow's 5 thoughts as Iowa football dominates 28-7 win over Purdue
item.description: IOWA CITY — Tim Lester’s third-and-10 play call was a screen pass all the way. No sense making a big mistake with the final seconds of the first half ticking away and with a chance to get into field-goal range from Purdue’s 44-yard line. Iowa left tackle Trevor Lauck and left guard Leighton Jones moved downfield to block immediately after the snap. And a swing pass from Hank Brown to Braeden Jackson was simple and smooth. Jackson turned that safe call into a mesmerizing 44-yard touchdown, weaving his way from the far left sideline to the right corner of the south end zone at Kinnick Stadium. A wall of wide-receiver blockers were waiting in Reece Vander Zee, Evan James and Tony Diaz … but they didn’t even need to do anything. Jackson’s sensational run had done most of the work, and suddenly a precarious Big Ten Conference football game was blown wide open. 44-YD TD FOR BRAEDEN JACKSON 🔥 @HawkeyeFootball Watch on NBC pic.twitter.com/OPHhEdBBgw — Big Ten Network (@BigTenNetwork) November 15, 2026 The score with 5 seconds left in the first half gave the Hawkeyes a 14-point advantage that held up for a needed 28-7 win on Nov. 14 before a 33rd-straight sellout crowd of 69,250 at Kinnick. Iowa’s touchdown drive of 11 plays and 83 yards in the two-minute drill produced a 21-7 halftime lead. Jackson’s meandering score was the kind of moment that can define a special season — not as awe-striking at Vander Zee’s walk-off touchdown catch at Michigan, but one of those winning plays that winning teams make in November. And the Jackson score doesn’t happen without a winning play from Brown earlier in the drive. After two ho-hum plays, Iowa faced a third-and-6 from its own 21. But Brown, who has known he can use his deceptively fast legs in spots to gain key yardage, dodged trouble and scooted forward for 11 hard-charging yards and a first down. He would rush for another first down (on second-and-4) on the drive, helping to set up the memorable Jackson TD. The Jackson score allowed Iowa to "double dip" to start the second half, as the Hawkeyes struck again on a 48-yard touchdown run from Xavier Williams just 3:53 into the third quarter for a 28-7 lead. That drive, too, was led by a smooth third-and-9 conversion from Brown to Vander Zee for 11 yards. Iowa converted 10 of its first 13 third-down tries. That was clutch against a Purdue offense that had some firepower behind quarterback Ryan Browne and scored 41 points on Minnesota, 38 on No. 4 UCLA and 36 on No. 13 Wake Forest. Xavier Williams takes it 48 yards to the house 🏠‼️ @HawkeyeFootball Watch on NBC pic.twitter.com/ZDXKAPhu2G — Big Ten Football (@B1Gfootball) November 15, 2026 Iowa was in total control of this game as a 17½-point favorite, in part thanks to the Jackson touchdown, moving to 8-2 overall and 5-2 in Big Ten play with two games to go. Iowa had no turnovers and punted only once, from Purdue's 37-yard line in the fourth quarter. The Hawkeyes' four touchdown drives went for 80, 66, 83 and 75 yards.

item.title: Report card grades say Purdue football is a massive failure at Iowa
item.description: IOWA CITY, Iowa — A six-hour bus ride got Purdue football to Iowa in plenty of time to get well rested for Saturday's kickoff. Unfortunately, it was the same Boilermaker team from the past three games on that bus, minus one coach. No. 15 Iowa (8-2) feasted on a Purdue team that's been plummeting since the mirage of a midseason uptick, defeating the Boilermakers 28-7 at Kinnick Stadium. Purdue's defense showed it needs more than a change at coordinator. The Boilermaker offense has seemingly vanished after so much early season promise. Here is our report card from a fourth-straight Boilermaker (3-7) loss. OFFENSE GRADE: F Remember when the Boilermakers went to Rose Bowl Stadium and hung 38 points on UCLA? That coming one week after scoring 36 against Wake Forest? Those two programs became this college football season's biggest success stories. Purdue, seemingly of equal offensive firepower if nothing else, has morphed into shell of its early season self. It might be time to scrap what worked then but clearly isn't now in favor of finding out what others are capable of. Wins and losses matter not at this stage. DEFENSE GRADE: F No Kevin Kane anymore to affix the blame to. The offense finally gave Purdue a shot in the arm late in the first half. The Boilermakers needed the defense to hold off Iowa for 1:42 to get into halftime trailing by seven. Instead, the Hawkeyes scored on a 44-yard swing pass to a running back on a third-and-10 with five seconds to go in a play that looked all too familiar to Maryland's 87-yard touchdown a week earlier. And Xavier Williams' 48-yard touchdown? Looked pretty similar to the 75-yarder Maryland ripped off a week ago. When you get deep into the fourth quarter and the opposing punter hasn't played, that's not a good thing. Maybe this wasn't so much a coordinator problem and more a personnel problem. SPECIAL TEAMS GRADE: D We witnessed a rarity early when Jacobo Echeverria Lozano hit the left upright on a 38-yard field goal attempt, just his second miss of the season. That could've given Purdue an early lead and momentum. It was a sign of things to come for the worst outing all season by Boilermaker special teams. By halftime, Purdue had one botched kickoff return attempt, another that was stuffed at the 16 and a fair catch interference penalty that preceded an eight-play Iowa touchdown drive. The only silver lining came when Keyshawn Burgos blocked a field goal in the fourth quarter. Otherwise, the Boilermakers couldn't even hang their hat on the one thing they've hung their hat on all year. COACHING GRADE: F Ryan Browne is a proven good running quarterback. item.title: Bryson DeChambeau Invests $125 Million In Clovis Golf Legacy
item.description: Jerod Ringwald-Imagn Images On Friday, November 13, Bryson DeChambeau revealed a huge scheme to construct an 18-hole golf course plus a residential area in his native Clovis, California. Spanning roughly 200 acres on the historic McFarlane Ranch, the site is located on the northeastern edge of Fresno. By linking the new golf course directly with homes for purchase, this development aims for a lasting legacy instead of a fast profit flip. Banking on a Small Town Instead of chasing stardom in metropolises such as Miami or Los Angeles like most golf celebrities, DeChambeau is reversing this trend by putting money into a municipality with roughly 120,000 residents. He informed reporters that a large share of his LIV Golf earnings is funding this development without outside investors. His 2022 entry into the Saudi-backed league, widely reported at about $125 million, provided the cash to reshape his local landscape. As other players concentrate on social media clips, he is constructing something tangible that people can walk on and live in. The plan fits the 33-year-old’s history perfectly. Before turning pro and studying physics at Southern Methodist University, he grew up in Clovis and went to Clovis East High School. The precision drive that helped him win the 2015 NCAA individual title is now being applied to design a course and a neighborhood. With nine victories during his PGA Tour career and five LIV Golf titles, he has the clout to lead a project of this size. A Down-to-Earth Approach People who have worked with DeChambeau say he brings a grounded attitude to the table. Oscar Parks, who is Head Professional at Sugarloaf Golf Club, described welcoming DeChambeau during a recent segment on The Drop Zone Show. During their time together, Parks observed that the group presented few lists or demands. “They were very professional and they didn’t waste a lot of time,” Parks explained in an interview, according to Yahoo Sports . He added that the group included only ordinary guys who did not require satin sheets or caviar for lunch. As DeChambeau considers his future in the sport, this new real estate venture arrives with his focus still on the community he knows. With over three million subscribers on his YouTube channel, his popularity as a content creator equals the fame he earned via his competitive golf career. Reflecting a simple goal to create a place for playing and building with people he knows, the project is named The Orchard Golf Club.

item.title: "Go home!' Michigan fans yelled at Kyle Whittingham after Oregon loss
item.description: EUGENE, OR − In a season that has been disappointing for a while and is starting to turn ugly, no moment was uglier than what unfolded just outside Oregon 's Autzen Stadium after Michigan football lost yet again. In one of the more jarring coach-fan interactions in recent Wolverines memory, Kyle Whittingham got booed and trash-talked − up-close − Saturday, Nov. 14, as he walked into, and then back out of, his postgame press conference. There, surrounding a long white tent where reporters awaited, a few dozen U-M fans, some of them holding signs about money (more on that in a moment), gathered along security ropes to heckle the Wolverines' coach. First, they booed, almost to his face. Then they yelled, screamed even: "Fire Whitt!" "Go home!" And: "Go back to Utah ... [expletive]!" It was harsh, and jarring, as if Twitter finally found its fleshy form. That they felt emboldened enough to holler such invective from a few feet away is a sign of the times, I suppose. It's also a state of the times, and a statement about the state of the program. It's listing, to be kind. Wobbling mightily, to be frank. In need of an overhaul? One way or another, to be sure, which was the message the fans had been waiting to directly impart. Oregon's 31-7 thrashing was U-M's fifth loss of the season and its second in a row. And while the Wolverines players showed some fight and pride, they continued to look in over their heads. This isn't their fault, and that's the problem . Though at least they appeared ready to play this week, a contrast from last Saturday's brutal showing against rival Michigan State. Whittingham stuck his foot in his mouth both before and after that rancid loss to the Spartans, and he tripped over himself again early last week. This time it wasn't about the school up the road ... or even the school down south. It was about the school out west, and it some will link his verbal missteps about Oregon's program to the way Oregon finished off the Wolverines. Which is to say ... Kyle Whittingham vs Dan Lanning ... they could've taken a knee. A few of them, if they'd wanted. They could've bled the clock and raised their arms and headed toward the tunnel and their coach, well, he could've walked to the big "O" in the middle of Autzen Stadium and extended a hand. Dan Lanning did that, of course, but not before he eschewed the knee ... or knees, when his Ducks got the ball one final time after Michigan turned it over one final time and his team got a first down. Instead of running it out, Lanning tried to run it forward, then run it forward again, then pass it forward and when that left Oregon at the Wolverines' 3-yard-line on fourth down with 43 seconds to go, yeah, he sent in his kicker for a field goal. That the Ducks' coach went for more points in a game his team had all but clocked away – they led 28-7 – will be seen, by some, as one coach giving another coach the bird. item.title: Clemson Spiral Deepens After Crushing Loss To Georgia Tech
item.description: Ashley Tumlin-Imagn Images Clemson football hit a new low on Saturday night. The Tigers fell 20-6 to a Georgia Tech team that had just fired four assistant coaches earlier in the week. This result marks the worst loss of the season for Dabo Swinney’s squad. The Yellow Jackets, sitting at 3-7, dominated the line of scrimmage while the home team in Clemson, South Carolina, could not move the ball. Georgia Tech rushed for 269 yards and scored two touchdowns on the ground. The Tigers managed only 228 total yards in the entire game. Clemson never previously lost to a squad with a losing record at kickoff during a 38-game streak until this defeat. It was the first time that happened since 2010. The starting quarterback was injured. Tait Reynolds left the game early with a leg injury after sliding on the third play. He needed help to get off the field and returned with a brace on his left knee. Backup Christopher Vizzina stepped in but struggled immediately. He finished 12-of-27 for 133 yards and threw an interception. Following the game, Vizzina also headed to the hospital due to an injury he sustained. The offense did not establish a rhythm without their starter. Clemson punted seven times and settled for just two field goals. Against Power Four opponents this season, the team has managed just five touchdowns across four home contests. Three of those came in a single win over North Carolina. Defensive Breakdown at Home The defense failed to stop the run, which was the main story of the night. On the ground, Georgia Tech averaged 5.2 yards per rush. Justice Haynes gained 116 yards rushing with a longest gain of 53 yards. Grady Adamson added 87 yards on 19 carries. Dabo Swinney addressed the failure directly after the game. “When you can’t stop the run, you don’t deserve to win,” Swinney said, according to CBS Sports . He admitted the team did not win the line of scrimmage. The Tigers did not record a single sack on the day. They forced six punts and got one interception, but that was not enough to stop the bleeding. The defense was unable to stop the Yellow Jackets’ ground game. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Stadium Emptying in Fourth Quarter Fans left the stadium early as the game slipped away. Georgia Tech coach Brent Key noticed the empty seats and liked what he saw. “And to finally look up and see the stadium emptying out (in the fourth quarter), that was good to see,” Key said. He had called the program one of the best in the country recently. “I said it during the week, this has been one of the premier programs in the league and the country for the last 12, 13 or 14 years now,” Key said. The crowd reaction speaks louder than any stat. “It’s frustrating; we’ve not played well (at home) coming off two really good wins,” Swinney said. He noted that the team had a great week of practice but it did not translate to the game. The home record is now 2-9 over the last 11 games against Power Four competition.
